About Peregrine
Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.

Our clients describe our support as “absolutely excellent” and our people as “instrumental to organization’s success.” Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair’s Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.

We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.

As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.
People first. Ownership always.
We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation come before competence. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.

At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.

At Peregrine Advisors, you will carry analytical questions for a federal agency from the data to a defensible, documented answer. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.

This is a remote position, although a hybrid arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area with openness to a variable commuting cadence is preferred. Wherever you work from, occasional travel to DC is part of the job. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.
Your first project
Your first project will likely have you transforming client data, structured, semi-structured, and unstructured, into analytic processes and outcomes that help drive mission-critical initiatives. Depending on the assignment, you may:

• Frame analytical questions with the people who own the mission, and turn them into designs that can actually be tested.

• Build analyses and models in Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) on cloud-native data platforms hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS).

• Build models that earn their place: forecasting, classification, risk scoring, and anomaly detection matched to the question, the data, and the scrutiny a federal decision has to survive.

• Design the evaluation that shows a model is fit for a client environment, with baselines, validation designs, error analysis, documented limits, and documentation that lets someone else verify your results.

• Build analytical features and datasets from large, messy, document-heavy corpora, including text extracted with Amazon Textract and analyzed with foundation models through Amazon Bedrock.

• Harden one-off notebooks into repeatable, reviewed analytical pipelines.

• Put findings in front of decision-makers in plain language, with visuals that carry the argument instead of decorating it.

• Use artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted analysis as standard practice, with language models and coding assistants across the lifecycle and your judgment on top.

Adaptability and a demonstrated capacity to learn new concepts, systems, and tools are what keep you ahead of program needs as projects complete and priorities shift.
Who you are
You are rigorous about method and honest about uncertainty: when the evidence supports a narrower claim, you make the narrower claim. You care what the data is for, not just what it contains, and you would rather spend a day understanding the process that produced a number than a week modeling it wrong. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.
What you bring

• A working command of statistics and machine learning applied to real operational data, not just curated coursework sets.

• The engineering habits that make analysis trustworthy: version control, reproducible pipelines, tested transformations, and documentation someone else can follow.

• The communication craft to make a technical result understandable to the people who depend on it.

• The precision to work where accuracy and auditability are not optional.

When we talk
Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned.
What we offer
You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.
What we commit to
As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.

We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

What are Trust Fund Positions?

Trust Fund positions are unique to the Smithsonian. They are paid for from a variety of sources, including the Smithsonian endowment, revenue from our business activities, donations, grants and contracts. Trust employees are not part of the civil service, nor does trust fund employment lead to Federal status. The salary ranges for trust positions are generally the same as for federal positions and in many cases trust and federal employees work side by side. Trust employees have their own benefit program, which may include Health, Dental & Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Transit/Commuter Benefits, Accidental Death and Dismemberment Insurance, Annual and Sick Leave, Family Friendly Leave, 403b Retirement Plan, Discounts for Smithsonian Memberships, Museum Stores and Restaurants, Credit Union, Smithsonian Early Enrichment Center (Child Care), Flexible Spending Account (Health & Dependent Care).

Conditions of Employment

• Pass Pre-employment Background Check and Subsequent Background Investigation for position designated.

• Complete a Probationary Period.

• Maintain a Bank Account for Direct Deposit/Electronic Transfer.

• The position is open to all candidates eligible to work in the United States. Proof of eligibility to work in U.S. is not required to apply.

• Applicants must meet all qualification and eligibility requirements within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement.

OVERVIEW
This position is located in Washington, DC, within the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO), Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI), under the Office of the Under Secretary for Science and Research at the Smithsonian Institution (SI).

STRI provides a global platform for research on tropical forests and marine ecosystems, biodiversity, and human well-being.

The ForestGEO program is a global network of scientists and forest research sites dedicated to advancing the long-term study of the world's forests.

The GEO-TREES initiative builds on this network to improve the accuracy and verification of global forest carbon estimates through collaboration among forest research sites worldwide. The Data Scientist supports the Forest Global Earth Observatory (ForestGEO) and GEO-TREES programs as a liaison between site-based data collection and the development of analytical data products.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Data Management, Scientific Analysis, and Software Programming (50%)

• Performs data-management, computational, and bioinformatics assignments supporting research in tropical biology, ecology, and forestry.

• Develops, implements, modifies, and maintains data-processing pipelines used to process plot-based tree inventory and related ecological data and to derive estimates such as forest woody biomass density.

• Evaluates the performance of existing data-processing pipelines and recommends modifications or improvements based on data characteristics, analytical requirements, user needs, and experience working with ForestGEO and GEO-TREES site teams.

• Develops and modifies computational procedures for analysis of ForestGEO and GEO-TREES scientific data using established data-science principles, methods, and practices.

• Processes, validates, organizes, and manages tree inventory, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), Airborne Laser Scanning (ALS), and Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) data for scientific analysis and long-term storage.

• Supports the archiving and long-term management of scientific datasets to ensure appropriate organization, documentation, accessibility, and usability.
